headline: COMET DRIFT got the LINK: chain your boosts to gold
lede: Re-seat a drift inside a live boost and the turbo doesn't just pay — it LINKS. The never-dry pick of the week turned the drift ladder into a combo economy: chained boosts run longer, ride faster, and seed the next tier so blue-violet-gold happens in one corner sequence.

notes.text: LINK x1..x3 shipped for COMET DRIFT GP and HD (#1690, PR #1693): each link extends the boost, lifts the top-speed ceiling +0.55u, and seeds 50% of the banked tier's charge into the next drift. Chains break honestly — drain, spin, or a cheap dump resets them.

The CPU field reads corners now: a rival's tier target rises one step when a bend is actually in its brake horizon (hairpins invite gold, sweepers pay blue early). Field tier-points are up 33-48% on every circuit, gold 2.5x at Corkscomb, and the pack's spin-rate is unchanged — faster karts, same drama.

cometcheck is GREEN at 403 gates: a rail rig drives the whole chain in simulation (x1 to x3, cap lift, drain and dump breaks), race-level floors prove the chain is alive in real GPs, and two new mutants (links-off, corner-blind) die on schedule. An in-browser real-key proof watched x1/x2/x3 fire on the live page.

Two harness laws learned the hard way: jalfern.com 308s to www, so prod verification must follow redirects (and game code lives in lazy index-*.js chunks); and the gh-shim now infers POST from -f bodies like real gh — it was silently wedging claim comments mid-lock.
